obscuraUnavailable.missing: Obscura is not installed, or not anywhere Proctor can see it. Proctor runs as a launchd agent, so it checks a fixed list of locations rather than a login shell's PATH; proctor_doctor reports every path it checked.
obscuraUnavailable.askThePerson: Proctor has no way to install it. Tell the person driving you rather than trying to install it yourself: the Proctor status window has the install command ready to copy for this Mac, and a Re-check that confirms it worked.

takeover.note: A foreground step says so on every display and leaves input alone. Set PROCTOR_TAKEOVER_INPUT=1 to have Proctor also hold the keyboard and mouse for the moments it is posting events; Esc stops a run while it does.

policy.note: Shape and posture only. The lists themselves, the filesystem roots, the trail's path and any key or token are deliberately not reported here: proctor_doctor is called before anything is established, and a health check is the wrong place to hand out configuration. This is a convention rather than a boundary — proctor_policy action "status" answers in full.

grants.howToFix: System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Accessibility, enable Proctor. On macOS 26 a managed fleet can also grant this by PPPC profile.
grants.name: Accessibility

grants.howToFix: System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording, enable Proctor. This grant can never be applied silently or by profile on any macOS version — a person has to click it.
grants.name: Screen Recording

grants.howToFix: Granted per target application the first time an Apple Event is sent, and not probeable in advance. If a declared-contract step fails with permissionAutomation, approve the prompt or enable the app under System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Automation ▸ Proctor.
grants.name: Automation

grants.howToFix: Granted. The input block can hold a person's keyboard while a run acts.
grants.name: Input Monitoring

lanes.note: Any one provider is enough. A person grants Accessibility and Screen Recording once inside the guest's GUI session, then clone reproduces the grants; nothing here provisions a guest as a side effect of a tool call, and this row locates the CLIs by reading the filesystem without running any of them. At most two macOS guests may run at once, which is Apple's rule rather than a Proctor setting; the pool and who holds it are reported beside this lane. Tahoe guests currently render no application windows (trycua/cua #870, Apple FB21748086); verify against Sequoia.
blockers: None of lume, prlctl or tart is usable on this machine, so there is no guest lane.

pools.reason: macOS on Apple silicon permits at most two concurrently running macOS guests per host. This is Apple's rule, not a Proctor setting.
